The study focused on maize (Zea mays L.) grown in various soil types, including sand, loamy sand, and sandy loam, under three irrigation treatments: full, medium, and low irrigation. The irrigation was managed based on soil moisture observations, and the total irrigation volume varied significantly among soil types due to differences in water-holding capacity. The experimental layout included nine plots for each soil type, with a total area of 20 m² per plot, and irrigation was controlled using water meters. Fertilizer application rates were standardized across treatments, and the maize was sown in April and harvested in September.
